headline: Islanders’ Stanley fined for slashing Devils’ Hischier
take:
Logan Stanley of the Islanders was fined for slashing Nico Hischier, Daily Faceoff reports, after he delivered multiple whacks on the Devils center during New Jersey's 5-4 overtime win on Saturday.

The fine matters less than what the numbers say about both players. Hischier has 7 goals in 17 games so far this season, almost exactly what his chances would predict (his goals are 0.23 below his expected goals, the measure of shot quality). With the Devils at 12-5-0, we see a center driving play: New Jersey has 62.55% of the expected goals when he is on the ice at five-on-five, and the team's share is 5.19 points better with him. Stanley is the more interesting case. He is averaging 21.27 minutes, and the Islanders have been better with him on the ice too (6.24 points better in their share of expected goals), though his five assists on zero goals fit a defender who creates little offense himself. Per Newsday-area beat coverage from NHL.com's Stefen Rosner, Stanley and Adam Pelech carried the penalty kill that night, a heavy role for a player now in the league's discipline file.
